Introduction

This will primarily cover canon Light Yagami’s (anime + manga + supplementary stuff). I write this primarily in response to what I believe the heavy downplay he’s been getting since really the series premier, like the people who claim that canon L low diffs him or the idea that Near vs Light is close. This contains analysis of his feats, explanations of his losses, and an analysis of his narrative, which I haven’t seen anyone done before.

Soichiro Yagami is dead. With few resources left, Mello briefly joins forces with Near, disclosing that the rule in the notebook about the owner having to kill within 13 days is fake. This plants the seeds of doubt into the task force, and Near furthers this by lying to them that Kira killed Mogi. Since the taskforce and the SPK were the only ones who knew about Mogi being there, and since Mogi could potentially disclose information on L, this almost certainly points to Kira being  a member of the task force. Aizawa meets with Near and tells him about the confinement of the new L and the second Kira.With this information and Soichiro’s words during the stunt to test if Kira/Kira 2 would kill him in the car - “I’ll kill Kira, and then kill myself,” Near deduces that Light Yagami is L.

Light identifies Misa as a weak point. Their investigation would lead to her, but he can’t kill her since it would be suspicious if she died. So Light needs to continue Kira’s reign from even more of a distance, originally from him directly, to Misa, and now to someone else. So Light searches for a proxy. While watching Sakura, Light finds a successor in a serious looking man, Teru Mikami

Reading him as someone loyal and devoted enough, Light pulls up his personal info and a short questionnaire he answered to see if he can act as Kira, and Light coldreads him as someone with very similar thinking to himself, someone who can act without constantly being fed information unlike Misa

. Ryuk arrives with the notebook for Mikami. In the anime, they have a slightly longer conversation where Ryuk states that “God” “singled out” and “chose” Mikami, knowing all of his personality and history. This was likely indirect manipulation at Light’s behest since Ryuk doesn’t ordinarily speak like that. As explained in Mikami’s backstory, he had a strong sense of justice and a fatalistic outlook on life, believing that her mother and bullies’ death was because of divine intervention. People Mikami wished would die soon even before Kira’s reign. When Kira came about, Mikami felt vindicated, believing God had truly been looking out for him. Light likely instructed Ryuk to appeal to Mikami’s sense of delusions of grandeur by having him address Kira as God and choosing language that would fluff his ego and keep him loyal - i.e. Mikami wasn’t just chosen out of convenience or a pawn, but personally selected after “God” had assessed his life and personality

. As for how Light could’ve known about this, it’s never stated, but we can assume it’s either intuition/EU/cold reading, or he used his resources to gather info on Mikami and profile him, which would still require EU but less so
As predicted, Aizawa begins investigating Misa and has the task force keep them under close watch,
but Misa’s already scheduled several criminals to die and passed her notebook to Mikami, who kills the greedy spokesperson Demegawa, much to Light’s approval.
However, Light knows he can’t let him freely kill for too long as even a slight gap in their ideals would inevitably show. He has to make contact sooner or later for course correction.
Mikami awaits Kira’s orders for 3 days before moving on his own to coincidentally pick Light’s ex-gf Takada as spokesperson for Kira.

Light knows that investigation into her would inevitably link back to him, but he also knows that if he was Kira, it’d be too obvious to pick his ex-girlfriend as spokesperson. He turns the coincidence to his advantage, coming clean about his past with her and convincing the task force to investigate the new spokesperson, allowing him to control Mikami through Takada

Light knows that he must be careful in seducing a powerful, prideful woman like Takada. He chooses his words carefully, pretending to be smitten, and meets with her under the pretense of the police secretly being Kira supporters awaiting orders.
The next meeting, Takada has fallen for Light and Mikami, as Kira, coincidentally calls, which Light takes advantage of.

He discreetly reveals that he is Mikami’s God, and that he’s under bugs and wires. For the task force, Light pretends that “Kira” has told him to get Takada’s pro-Kira bodyguards to search the room for wires, so Light has no choice but to remove them. This allows Light to reveal to Takada that he is Kira and establish a communication system: Light will write notes to Takada during their meetings, Takada will call Mikami. Furthermore, now he has direct control over Kira’s spokesperson in advancing his ideology; this prevents any further deviations such as Mikami targeting unproductive people. Some time afterwards, he has Mikami send pages of the Death Note to Takada, making sure that Mikami disguises them as fanmail.

Takada and Light meet up regularly, ostensibly pushing the investigation forward. Due to Near’s meddlings, the task force has grown suspicious of Light, so Light has given them this red herring to keep them under his heel and to facilitate communication with Mikami (X-Kira). Even with Hal Lidner having infiltrated Takada’s inner circle, this allows Light to control the narrative and move his plan forward right under her nose. Near all but knows Kira is L/Light Yagami,

In such a situation, he has no care for Takada beyond not letting any evidence of her being a Kira spill beyond him, and the order to kill criminals serves two purposes: it serves as a tell for Mikami, who Light had (unfortunately in error) anticipated that Mikami would write her name in the fake notebook to make it seem legit, and it also buys time for Light and Mikami. Light writes her name in the scrap at 2:32, January 26 forcing her to destroy all evidence of her working as Kira lest Near use it against him. The SPK, The task force, Light, and Near meet up at the warehouse, both parties enacting their grand plan. Near forces everyone to wait an extra hour to make sure that no one is under the notebook’s control. Near then elaborates that he’s waiting for X-Kira, who will write all of their names in his notebook. X-Kira has been filling one page a day, so Near just counted the days ahead to the day of the meeting and replaced that page and subsequent pages. Light’s counter was the plan outlined below. Near further countered that after Mello’s intervention. When Takada was kidnapped, Mikami figured that Kira couldn’t act or make any moves and knew Takada had to be killed, so he used the real notebook to kill her, exposing Light’s plan when Gevanni tailed him. The two groups proceed to the warehouse, Light is exposed and freaks out, bluffs (or he might’ve been telling the truth) that the notebook the task force had may’ve been switched, before getting gunned down by Matsuda while trying to go for the scrap hidden in his watch.
So, Light’s endgame strategy can be summed up as:
Set up the proxy, X-Kira, to continue his judgement as Kira to counter Near subtly turning the task force’s attention inwards
Figure out Near will discover X-Kira

Continually deceive the task force with “progress” of the investigation. Since Takada is a spokesperson for Kira, the prospect of gaining info from her is too attractive, even with their suspicions of Light, so this facilitates communication with Mikami

Feed Near fake information to bait him into focusing on Mikami as the Kira killing people (confirming a shinigami doesn’t possess Mikami, Mikami “killing” people in public with the fake notebook, the names and dates on Mikami’s notebook lining up with dead criminals so it can hold up under data analysis, having Mikami state that there’s no shinigami trailing him so that Near feels confident), inducing him into creating a logical plan to expose Light

Knowing how Near thinks (his desire to personally defeat Kira, his need as a lawman to prove without doubt that Light = Kira, his low willingness to act), create a fake notebook and keep Ryuk away from Mikami to instill him with confidence when he swaps it out
Give Mikami instructions to “confirm it” with Takada over phone when Near does the swap, having him inspect the notebook every night to recognize it
All the while, have Takada do all the killings
Play along with Near’s plan. Instruct Mikami the date that Near wants to reveal Light is Kira, and have him use the real notebook, which he’d kept hidden, on that day to kill everyone
Include various countermeasures here and there (the confirmation email, Takada knowing what to say in the event that she gets captured, the other notebook swap (?), etc.)
This strategy has the effect of:
Furthering the spread of Kira’s ideology through Takada
Continuing his creation of the New World as criminals keep dying
Countering his own task force’s growing suspicion, using them as an alibi while the killings continue
Facilitating covert lines of communication between Light, X-Kira, and Takada by using the task force’s drive to catch Kira against them
Casting suspicion off Light by giving him a constant alibi under task force surveillance to the SPK
Logically and psychologically manipulating Near into thinking he’s figured out Light’s scheme and come up with his own, which will make him confident enough to come out of hiding
Misleading the task force
Putting Light in position to kill every last one of his opponents in one fell swoop with a counter plan
And it lasts roughly 3 months from November (Soihiro’s death) to January (Light’s death).

“Light underestimated Near”

This is a common myth that gets thrown around by everyone from scd members to casual fans: Light lost because he got cocky, complacent, and he underestimated Near. In fact, the exact opposite is true. Light, despite never having met Near until their final showdown, has a perfect understanding of Near’s character. Near has Hal Lidner become a candidate for being Takada’s bodyguard. This is a trap, since the other members of the task force know that Hal is with the SPK, so if she dies, while posing as a Kira worshipper bodyguard, then Light is implicated as he ostensibly shouldn’t know that Hal is with the SPK. Light instantly sees through this, reasoning that Near undoubtedly did not reveal his whereabouts to Hal, in case Light used the book to control her, and that Near made it obvious so Light would single her out.
While conversing with Takada after Misa was kidnapped, Takada states how Kira answers her addresses to him on TV through emails that also contain kill lists.

Light states he could figure out Kira’s age, the characteristics of the region he’s in, and his mental state. Of course, this is a fake conversation, but Light is stating what he, as an experienced investigator, can ostensibly do.

Matsuda confirms this based off his help during the Yotsuba arc. This is a bit of an aside, but this just shows how good Light is at reading people. Light passes a note to Takada instructing her to text him, “I want to see you,” when T (X-Kira) tells her “I’ve confirmed it.”
Light states that everything is moving as he has foreseen it.

It’s a message that could easily pass as a lover’s to a beloved, but it’s in fact a signal informing Light when X-Kira’s fake notebook has been altered by Near. Near begins putting his plan into action, but first waiting over 3 weeks after Gevanni first touched Mikami’s (fake) notebook to make sure he wasn’t being controlled. Gevanni’s safe, Near proceeds, and Light gets the text. He states that he knew from the very beginning what Near’s plan would be and awaits Near.
He knew Near would deduce the existence of X-Kira, and he knew would narrow it down to Mikami.

Given how convoluted the reasoning process was, it is actually very impressive that Light gauged his intelligence like that. This can also buff Light’s reasoning abilities as well. He states that he “assumed” Near would find Mikami, but he also states that he “assumed” Near’s plan before going into his logical thought process behind it that predicted Near’s reasoning. Summary:
Light’s EP/EU:

Having never met Near, only having conversed through a distorted communication system, Light perfectly understood just how smart he was, his pride, his obsession, his caution, and the method he would use to catch Light months before he even created that method.

Light’s reasoning abilities are also superior to Near not just because he made the same deductions as Near did with the swap plan, but he also had to engage in theory of mind to do so. Even more so if you think he similarly reverse engineered the X-Kira deduction.
Light’s Theory of Mind Feat Analysis
Light’s entire final gambit relies on him knowing exactly what Near would do. What is that exactly? After finding Mikami, apparently the Kira doing the killings,

Near planned to incriminate Light by baiting Light into a situation that would present the prime opportunity for him to finish everyone off with Mikami damningly leaving Light out in the massacre, but Near would swap the pages of the planned date of that meeting and all subsequent pages to keep everyone safe.
To figure that out, Light engaged in very heavy theory of mind (hence the title), assessing what Near knew, what Near wanted, and how Near thought, to deduce what Near would do.

This will consider only the information Light had access to in order to form his premises and is based primarily on stuff Light says in his internal monologue with some gaps reasonably and necessarily filled here and there to account for the preciseness with which he figured out Near’s plan.
The feat
Near wants to personally defeat Kira with hard proof (a confession or catching Kira in the act)
Near is unwilling to simply kill Kira
Light would never confess
So Near plans to catch Kira red-handed with the murder weapon
Near will find Mikami, who also has a notebook
The situation where Kira uses the notebook mustn’t harm anyone
Since the task force has one, and Mikami has the other, Near will target Mikami as the easiest one to go for (Abductive)
With knowledge of the notebook, there can only be a situation where Light or Mikami attempt murder via writing names in the notebook
Light has no access to the notebook as it’s under task force watch
So Near will engineer a situation using the notebook so that Mikami will be implicated for attempted murder, but without any threat to the would-be victims
The simplest way to do this would be to switch the lethal page corresponding to the day (a -right sided page) of the meeting and all subsequent pages with fake ones (Abductive)
However, Mikami is intelligent and ascetic
So if Near just switches the pages, it’s likely Mikami would spot the switch (Abductive)
Near would anticipate and likely try and counter this (Abductive)
So Near will probably go the extra mile and not just switch out the pages (Abductive)
The simplest route would be to forge the handwriting of his previous kills somehow (Abductive)
But even if Mikami attempts murder in that situation, that does not cast suspicion on Light. To do so, he has to leave one person out.
Mikami’s killing patterns as Kira were different because of his slightly different ideals and his shinigami eyes
Near, again, would likely spot this since he’s intelligent and, with existing knowledge on the case, would know about the shinigami eyes (Abductive)
So Near’s plan hinges on Light being incriminated when his name is left out in Mikami’s attempted massacre that can only occur if the Kira that attempts it has shinigami eyes
If we break it up into syllogisms…
Syllogism Set 1: Near’s Objective
Premise 1:
Near wants to defeat Kira with hard proof, such as a confession or catching him in the act.
Premise 2:
Light will never confess.
Conclusion:
Therefore, Near must catch Kira in the act to obtain hard proof.
Syllogism Set 2: Near’s Constraints
Premise 1:
Near is unwilling to simply kill Kira.
Premise 2:
The only alternative is capturing Kira in a way that produces incontrovertible proof.
Conclusion:
Therefore, Near seeks a scenario where Kira exposes himself without harming anyone.
Syllogism Set 3: The Notebook Strategy
Premise 1:
Mikami possesses a Death Note.
Premise 2:
The task force possesses the other notebook.
Premise 3:
Near needs to set a trap that avoids harm but catches Kira acting.
Conclusion:
Therefore, Near will target Mikami as the more accessible suspect to bait a trap involving the notebook.
Syllogism Set 4: The Setup
Premise 1:
The Death Note only works when a name is written inside.
Premise 2:
Light has no access to the notebook.
Conclusion:
Therefore, if a name is written, it must be Mikami who wrote it.
Syllogism Set 5: Engineering a Harmless Attempt
Premise 1:
Near needs an attempted murder that does not result in death.
Premise 2:
Switching the relevant Death Note pages with fake ones is the simplest way to prevent harm.
Conclusion:
Therefore, Near must engineer a notebook swap that renders the notebook ineffective without Mikami realizing.
Syllogism Set 6: Anticipating Mikami’s Intelligence
Premise 1:
Mikami is intelligent and disciplined
Premise 2:
An obvious switch of notebook pages would be noticed by Mikami.
Conclusion:
Therefore, Near must disguise the fake pages convincingly.
(Abductive)
Syllogism Set 7: Forging the Pages
Premise 1:
A convincing forgery must imitate Mikami’s past entries.
Premise 2:
The best way to disguise the switch is to mimic Mikami’s handwriting and patterns.
Conclusion:
Therefore, Near will likely forge the fake pages with Mikami’s handwriting.
Syllogism Set 8: Linking Mikami’s Actions to Light
Premise 1:
Mikami’s killings differ from Light’s in pattern (being able to kill criminals without names broadcasted) and ideology.
Premise 2:
Mikami possesses shinigami eyes; Light does not.
Premise 3:
Near knows about the shinigami eyes.
Conclusion:
Therefore, Near will take advantage of Mikami’s shinigami eyes..
Syllogism Set 9: The Final Incrimination
Premise 1:
If Light’s name is missing from a mass execution list, it is suspicious
Premise 2:
Mikami would only exclude Light if he believed Light was Kira.
Conclusion:
Therefore, the exclusion of Light’s name in a failed kill list implicates him as Kira.
Abductive:
Mikami could only reasonably do this if he was concealed, otherwise he’d get shot
The location of the meeting would therefore need to be an isolated place with as few windows and doors as possible

L Mind Reading

With Light and Misa exonerated, a depressed L explained that he had no choice but to conclude Light was innocent, having merely been under Kira’s control and forced to make himself seem like Kira. But that would also mean that when Light turned himself in, he was a Kira. And when the powers passed onto someone else, he lost his memories - all under the real Kira’s control.
Much later, after making breakthroughs in catching the new Kira thanks to Light, L offers Light the position of being L should he die, attempting to manipulate him. Light quickly sees through this.
One, they had previously made a vow (mostly Light), that as long as they were chained, they would die together. If Kira killed L, he would certainly kill Light as well.

Next, He explains that L has assumed two possibilities: Light is still Kira, but faking otherwise; or that Light (and this is L’s vague piecing together of the memory loss plan) had set things up such that someone else would be Kira, exonerating Light, until eventually the notebook returned to the memory-wiped Light somehow. In either case, Light knew L never even entertained the possibility that he was innocent, despite all evidence to the contrary. He further accurately identifies why L would even offer Light the position of L - that is, because it would be the ultimate power move. Light would be incredibly incentivized to accept that seemingly innocent offer, and his success with Yotsuba even gave him the cover to accept it without coming off as suspicious, which L took advantage of. “To gain the position of L and be able to freely control the police around the world while being Kira behind the scenes. That would be the ultimate position.” This all impresses even L, who thinks “Amazing to know what I’m thinking that accurately.”

The fabricated diary that concludes with Light stating he might be Kira and Light supposing he might have been possessed by a shinigami in his sleep play into this. Given the already extraordinary circumstances surrounding the case, L can’t not consider that there might be validity to this theory. This acts as another layer of fortification for the exoneration since now, even if Light and Misa have heavy circumstantial/forensic evidence against them, then they could never be held accountable since they were under supernatural possession. This possibility actually makes L depressed. And to shield that, Light waited 7 days to stealthily give up the Death Note while in confinement. The killings had stopped immediately after he was thrown in jail, but he waited a long time to lose his memories. Why?

It’s likely that Light attempted to time his contradiction in personality (from stoically accepting confinement and wanting L to keep him there no matter what he says to desperately begging to be released) to around when he thought Rem would discover a new person to act as Kira. He was off by one week. But the idea was that if the contradiction coincided with the resurgence of killings, then it would indeed seem like some evil spirit had left Light and found a new host. As for the contradiction, the instruction Light gave to L to, no matter what, not release him shields the contradiction and his exoneration. It’s harder to dismiss Light’s change in personality as just anger or madness from confinement if he directly goes against something he said earlier so clearly, which the memory-wiped Light just dismisses as him being previously crazy earlier (again, lending to the possession supposition). It also adds another layer to his exoneration. The task force were loyal to Light’s word and withheld pressuring L to release Light, which only built tension as more and more criminals continued to die.

Finally, Higuchi’s death plays into Greater Kira Theory and adds yet another layer to obfuscate any suspicion towards Light and Misa. When Higuchi was captured, he immediately died. With the consideration of another Kira, then it seems like a tactical move to prevent Higuchi from spilling any information. (Thus, this theory also has the effect of concealing the benefits Light gained from killing Higuchi, casting suspicion elsewhere.) It would then be reasonable to consider that Greater Kira kills Kiras who get caught ASAP. Given that neither Light nor Misa died after capture and after they were freed, it would seem like Greater Kira didn’t fear them spilling any info, further obfuscating whether they were even Kira or not, i.e. if they were Kira, then Greater Kira would have killed them; but even if they were Kira, they couldn’t be held culpable due to supernatural possession. Light’s masterful execution of Higuchi while sitting right next to L clinches this, as, since L couldn’t discover Higuchi’s name in the notebook, the only one at the scene as far as L knows with the only murder weapon that could’ve caused Higuchi’s death, then it’s something he had to consider. Though to L’s own credit, he does make the deduction in seconds of getting the notebook that there were two notebooks on Earth, so he’s only somewhat fooled.

This possibility drives L into depression for quite some time, with Light seemingly having changed the rules of the game entirely after his confinement. But his intuition so he still feels certain that Light is Kira. Against anyone else, this would’ve been extremely confounding, and the possibility of a Greater Kira only remains a troubling uncertainty in L’s mind once he gets his hands on the notebook.
Effectiveness and Execution:

To start, the Memory Recall required, as detailed in another analysis, an extremely high threshold of cognition and emotional strength to pull off the plan smoothly. Anyone lesser than Light would be too overwhelmed, confused, braindead, or mentally conflicted to kill Higuchi as he did. But the presence of L makes it exponentially more difficult given the detective’s power of perception and observation. To kill Higuchi would therefore require an absurdly high level of composure and sleight of hand. Lastly, taking over as L also required immense intellect in several ways from deduction to engineering (detailed in another document).

The obvious victories of the plan are that it brought his holistic strategy to fruition, simultaneously killing his only equal and taking over as L, but it also erased the new problems that had arisen, Misa’s incrimination and Rem, who protected Misa and threatened to kill Light. The plan leaves Light free to kill Misa at his discretion. It also achieves more subtle victories. It secures Light’s position on the task force. Before that, he was on shaky ground with them, but making progress with catching Higuchi demonstrated his worth and intellect. It completely bypassed L’s own preparations that made his death implicate Light by allowing a shinigami to be discovered and cornering her into blatantly killing L. Having the wherewithal to go for Rem’s notebook after she died, also good execution on Light’s part, also gave Light his own notebook to use. With the only other known notebook in their possession and having combed through Light’s place, Light would have a further alibi to keep killing as Kira. And one last coverage, Light knew he had to kill L fast. L had a feeling soon after Misa’s killing spree that Light had him cornered. If he fled or retreated with the Death Note, Light knew, it would be suspicious for Rem to hang around there. It would beg the question who she was possessing.
Truly a “perfect victory.”
Holistic Analysis:

Light’s entire strategy in the first half of the series is a brilliant mix of offense and defense. The offense aspect can be thought of as drawing L more and more out of hiding while also gradually limiting the moves he can make.
Concentrating his killings in Japan soon after the broadcast trap forces
L to focus his attention on Japan and work with the Japanese police
He is now dependent on them, and must therefore also maintain some sort of relationship with them.
Light uses information from the police, showing he has a connection to them
L is forced either to investigate them, setting himself up to compromise their relationship, or ignore the information leak, giving Kira an advantage
L investigates discreetly to maintain his relationship through the FBI
but the FBI get massacred, revealing L’s deception and scaring away most investigators
L is forced to either reveal himself to rebuild trust with the few detectives brave enough to remain or possibly lose all his eyes and ears in Japan.
With Kira having demonstrated that he will kill tails and the massacre of law enforcement acting as a strong fear-based deterrent,
L is forced to rely on a safer hands-off surveillance strategy
The prime Kira suspect (Light), if he is Kira, seemingly evades surveillance effortlessly.
With Kira having demonstrated a willingness to kill tails and an ability to bypass hands-off surveillance,
L is forced to again pursue a direct “keep your enemies close” approach, albeit heavily fortified, to apply as much pressure as possible and possibly trick the suspect into killing
Light is now on the task force.

Looking at it this way, we can see that Light brought L down from a shadowy operative commanding the world’s police and media through a screen while hidden far away in a dark room to an investigator forced to work alongside his #1 suspect with a team that’s count didn’t even hit the double digits.  L has a few subtle victories here and there - surprising Light at the ceremony, the card trick (if you shut your brain off), and his handling of the second Kira - but for most of his battle against Light he was playing right into the latter’s hands. We can see this with how Light anticipates several of his moves. He had the alarm system to warn him of any tails, he had the potato chip and porn magazines ready for the surveillance strategy, and he saw through the second broadcast trap with ease.

More impressively, he adapts everything the story throws at him (L’s attacks, Rem, Misa, etc.) to his advantage. Even the first move made by L, the Lind L. Taylor trap, Light turned to his advantage by responding with a killing spree in Japan that played into the semi-false profile (explained later) that Light caused L to form, which later would play into the “L Do You Know” misdirection to conceal the FBI massacre. The potato chip strategy and FBI massacre showed L that surveillance was useless, but the false profile gave L hope that Light could be made to slip up in another emotional mistake, causing him to form the self revelation strategy, which has the advantage of fully closing the distance between them.

L’s biggest stunt came after the FBI massacre. By then, he had gotten a grasp of Kira’s strategy of closing the distance between them and decided to use that to his advantage. L had logically concluded that neither an indirect approach with tails or cameras would do, that he had to be well-guarded given the risks, that he needed to make Light slip up some compromising information, and so he surprised Light at the ceremony. Since Light had profiled L as someone who did his best to remain anonymous, aloof, and distant, and L’s previous strategies had reflected that accurately, L directly approaching him was something he was genuinely blindsided by. It’s likely that Light instead thought that L would opt to recruit him through some sort of proxy, not via direct contact. A good move that makes him for a while unkillable. It briefly turns Light’s own strategy against him. While Light only countered this later on, he played his cards well such that L ultimately got nothing besides fortifying his position.

And that brings us to the Memory Loss Plan. Just to immediately get this out of the way, it’s perhaps Light’s best moment of improvisation/adaptability, going from being almost cornered by Rem and L’s to killing them both with his master plan, among several other numerous victories that it accomplishes. Since Light was so good at evading any directly incriminating traps, the most L managed against him was circumstantial evidence, though very suspicious evidence - that Kira #2 had left an implicit hint to meet at Aoyama on the 22nd, confirmed seeing Kira #1 on the 23rd, and that Light was in Aoyama on the 22nd + the Raye Penber stuff. Memory Loss Plan was always a defensive measure he could come up with to exonerate himself against any circumstantial evidence L could find. In fact, it’s hinted at after Soichiro’s heart attack when Light suggests confinement to make L trust him, showing that Light already considered such a possibility. And even if you think it wasn’t fully formed, there’s no reason to believe Light couldn’t formulate if he was caught in similar but different damning circumstances. This includes the other examples of “luck” people commonly charge against Light. Naomi says Raye revealed his identity to one of his tails (Light)? Raye reports the bus incident to his superiors, and L reveals Raye revealed his ID to Light? It would inevitably be countered by some version of Memory Loss, albeit without Rem to kill L. Thus, it functions as the ace up his sleeve defense against anything short of direct evidence, but the canon version also acted as offense.

With the run down over the strategy complete, it’s important to analyze the more minute, nuanced areas that contributed to his strategy. Light gave 2 characters to consider: the ace student, all-around nice guy Light Yagami, and the childish super-killer Kira. Everyone knows the first is a facade. Light studies frequently, has perfect grades, has friends, and is seemingly the perfect son and brother. He’s helped solve two cold cases in the past, and it’s even established early on that he plans to rise to the top of the NPA. He idolizes his father, undoubtedly the most moral person in the show, and observes that the Kira case is taking a serious toll on Soichiro, and he promises to personally put Kira behind bars if Soichiro dies. These details subtly plan the seeds for Light to close the distance between him and L without acting as Kira. His career aspirations will inevitably put him within L’s sphere of influence (the NPA) within 1-2 years, and his father he utilizes to give himself an emotional reason to take on the case, both humanizing him and giving him another reason to join the case. It’s best seen when Soichiro has a heart attack, Light immediately feigns panic and shouts that it’s Kira, and brings up his promise in front of L later in a “corny” display.

I’ve hinted at it before, but the “childish and hates to lose” profile of Kira that L has wasn’t completely accurate. L had profiled Kira as a young person around the age of a student prior to the broadcast trap, young enough to be idealistic, old enough to not be afraid of the Death Note. The broadcast trap produced an emotional response from Kira in response to being called “evil,” a childish outburst. Through the power of introspection, Light knew from his past actions and from his understanding of how L would interpret such actions, how L would profile Kira, hence Light being able to exactly replicate L’s profile of Kira when the latter asked him to. Light played into this with the killing spree concentrated in Japan. In the context of someone who just suffered a humiliating defeat and is likely a young idealist, then it does seem like an emotional outburst, revealing a very competitive side in response to a loss, but that, as previously said, conceals the strategic aspect of it. He purposefully committed murders around the time frame of a student then blatantly switched the pattern when the police caught on. That (1) plays into the “childish” personality as it seems like a taunt directed to L, (2) foreshadows the “L Do You Know” misdirection. From L’s POV, it seems like another message to L, but more communicative given the actual words. L is tricked into focusing on the notes, causing him to be blindsided when the FBI drop dead. And the final suicide note that L receives after the FBI agents’ deaths further plays into this, forming the message “L Do You Know Gods of Death Love Apples.” It’s useless. Kira was trolling L like a child. Later, Light not so subtly calls L dumb when he tries a second trick with a fake broadcast, showing another seemingly emotional, foolish moment. While L gets an understanding of Kira’s strategy after some introspection and that he’s very cunning, he’s still convinced of the profile. This leads him to believe that he may be able to force emotional mistakes if he applies enough pressure, leading him to reveal himself to Light. Since Light’s resolve was stronger than L believed, Light is able to maintain his cool completely, no-selling the offensive aspect of L’s strategy.

That’s not to say L was wholly off. Light does clearly get pissed when he feels he’s lost, but Light just flanderized it in order to make L feel safer risking strategies based around this profile. He was wholly self aware of how others would perceive his true personality and knew how to strategically utilize it to his benefit in order to make L make mistakes and underestimate Light. And by the time of the tennis scene, it does seem that both have a greater understanding of each other, with L knowing that Light knows of his profile of Kira. And the two engage in several layers of “I know that you know that I know…”

But of the two, Light does seem to engage in a greater degree of metacognition with a greater understanding of his opposition. We see this in his constant usage of throwing dilemmas that force L into lose-lose positions based around his aloof, pragmatic, and logical personality. L can either investigate the police or allow the information leak, L goes behind their backs; L can either reveal himself to the police to retain his allies in a risky move or attempt to rebuild resources more slowly, L goes for the former; L can either keep Light Yagami close - allowing more direct surveillance and pressure - or keep him afar to keep himself safe, L chooses the riskier option to make progress; and the Memory Loss Plan is filled with these. Ultimately, past the first move made by L, Light heavily strategically outmaneuvered him, with the latter playing right into his hand. When L tried to exploit his understanding of Kira, we see that the attempts largely fall flat, with direct pressure yielding no hint of fear or anxiety for L to pick up on. It’s no wonder that a few moments before his death L intuits that Light has turned the tables on him, and at that moment L was the moment under Light’s gaze.

And for fairness sake, I’ll quickly go over his blunders. As I’ve said, I don’t believe any of these would’ve sunk him due to the confinement strategy he had, but still errors are errors. Note: This doesn’t count bad luck. (1) Realistically, Light’s bus hijacking plan would’ve been reported to Raye’s superiors. Light could’ve easily planned around this by simply scheduling Raye to die when he did but stating that he doesn’t discuss the incident with anyone. (This would’ve also saved him from the Naomi situation. (2) Anime only: Light considers the notecard scene a loss within his mental monologue, but this is still very inconsequential short of him outright confessing. (3) Light pursuing Kira #2 proves to be damning later on. L deduces that Kira 1 and Kira 2 made contact on the date that Light volunteered to go to Ao, but he was in a bad situation either way as he did have to get Kira #2 under control but couldn’t really have done so since Misa had planned out finding Light well. L’s strategy of turning Light’s own strat against him genuinely pays off well. (4) Light fails to anticipate that L would turn his own strategy against him. (5) When Light has Misa send her final tape to the station, he doesn’t have it thoroughly cleansed of forensic evidence, which gets her caught. These are the 5 notable mistakes Light made. Considering it’s a battle that spans several months, this isn’t too bad.
I’ll give a quick run down of the various categories:
Adaptability

- Adapts all of L’s moves against him - surveillance strat, FBI, profile, etc. The strat most impressively also adapts to Misa’s interference and Rem’s ultimatum, turning it into a two birds with one stone against both of them.
Effectiveness

- Achieves all of Light’s goals. Manipulates L into a strategy that ultimately proved to be his downfall. Other victories include crippling the investigation via FBI massacre and successfully making L underestimate him.
Alignment
- Each counteraction draws L closer and closer towards him. Fake profile draws directly into suicide note misdirection and later when Light calls out the second broadcast as dumb.
Fortitude -

Memory Loss obviously serves as a major contingency plan against any sort of circumstantial evidence against Light, which itself is loaded with contingencies. Other aspects of this include Light making sure that L couldn’t get any major difference in temporal pattern during the potato chip killings, the suicide note misdirection, etc.
Resilience -
Light most impressively overcomes Misa and Rem, who put him in a situation where he was effectively cornered. Getting rid of Naomi on the fly is also impressive.
Shielding

- Memory Loss. Light’s general strategy of forcing dilemmas on L has the effect of either closing the gap between them, increasing the risk to L, or keeping Light at a distance, where he can more easily evade anything L throws at him.
Execution -
Light’s superb acting skills during surveillance strat and L’s self reveal. His general composure. Memory Recall. Him actually winning.
Feat Framework:
External Situation:

First, as Light mentions at the start of the series, he has to maintain his grades and study fastidiously as he previously did. It plays into his long term goal of joining the NPA, an alternate contingency plan to get close to L, it plays into his main plan of joining the task force as it’s a very blatant indicator of his intellect to L, and it shields his innocent “Light Yagami” persona. If Soichiro informed L that Light’s grades or behavior changed noticeably around the advent of Kira’s reign, then L would have more reason for suspicion. Second, Light has to maintain a convincing facade of an innocent, precocious high schooler around trained detectives who are after him, letting no signs of stress, anxiety, nor deception slip through; this becomes particularly egregious when L observes him for hours on end through surveillance cameras, even ambushes him at the graduation ceremony to apply pressure, but can’t arouse any sort of reaction in him.
Opponent Quality:

L. While his brilliance is well known, people overestimate how far he got because of it. L was a billionaire who was able to casually have a multi-story building built merely to act as a temporary HQ for the case, he had command over the FBI until Light’s machinations set them apart, he had dozens of detectives who could perform the more hands-on work of forensics for him -  and they also acted as his eyes and ears - and his anonymity served as the perfect counter to Light’s Death Note. It’s fitting that Light was up against such a massive force, as he would obviously run circles around any ordinary government threat.
Internal Situation:

Light’s biggest advantage is the Death Note, a supernatural weapon that can kill anyone with just a name and a face. Via clever usage of the information he knows about it and its ability to murder and puppeteer people, he matches the other greatest mind on Earth, L Lawliet. An underrated aspect of Light’s performance is that he is constantly nerfed throughout the series. Just using the note requires immense mental strength. In Death Note: Short Stories, it’s shown that a later Kira was catatonic after using the Death Note for 3 days, and he eventually committed suicide after Near called him out. More than that, multiple times it’s mentioned that the Death Note is a curse upon its user, bringing misfortune to them, so Light in fact had in-universe bad luck throughout the series, making it very impressive how much he accomplished.

One final thing. What was Light’s plan, after closing the distance between them,  to secure the kill on L before Misa and Rem came along? He seems to have in mind a broad strategy of getting close to L and manipulating information out of him that Light could use to discover his name.
If we bare in mind the Memory Loss plan, he might’ve had some concepts of a plan involving another Kira with the eyes, but we’ll never know.
